not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The closest L1 analog with direct absolute bioavailability evidence, imipramine-N-oxide, showed 100% systemic availability after oral dosing versus IV in healthy volunteers, supporting high oral bioavailability in the tricyclic dibenzoazepine series.

L4 records for the close analog oxcarbazepine show essentially complete absorption after a single oral radiolabeled dose in humans (C147), almost complete absorption after oral tablets (C109), and classification as highly permeable in mouse jejunum Ussing-chamber studies (C106).

L3 records after oral carbamazepine dosing show measurable systemic exposure of its metabolite carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide: AUC0-120 120.7 µmol·h/L after a single 200 mg oral dose (C76), Cmax 2.1 µmol/L (C85), and AUC12 9.98 µg·h/mL at steady state (C97), consistent with oral absorption of carbamazepine.

L5 Caco-2 bidirectional data for the tricyclic analog imipramine show Papp A-B 10.8 × 10^-6 cm/s, Papp B-A 12.1 × 10^-6 cm/s, efflux ratio 1.1 (C148, C151, C184), high absorption (C183), and no change in P-gp-mediated efflux with taurocholate (C191), indicating no significant gut-wall efflux in this scaffold.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement (oral vs IV) for carbamazepine itself is present in the supplied records.
L5 gut-wall efflux records are for imipramine and other molecules, not carbamazepine; transfer is inferred from tricyclic scaffold similarity.
L4 absorption/permeability records are for oxcarbazepine, not carbamazepine.
L3 exposure records lack IV comparators, so they inform absorption but do not quantify F.
Some L1/L2 records are from cirrhosis or fed conditions and may not match a general healthy adult oral condition.

No affirmative threshold-relevant evidence supports F < 20%.
